newsitem.title: UK: BP shares gain amid renewed U.S. interest.
newsitem.headline: BP shares gain amid renewed U.S. interest.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum Co Plc rose on Tuesday on the back of an upsurge in U.S. interest that had already driven its American Depositary Shares to an all-time high on Monday, traders said.

Dealers said the share was being driven higher primarily by U.S. interest, partly linked to a recent visit to the U.S. by chief executive John Browne which included meetings with U.S. investors. BP shares were up 9.5 pence at 684.5 pence at 1119 GMT, while the FTSE 100 was down 4.8 points 3,957.3.
Traders said there were also signs of switching into BP and out of Shell Transport & Trading, down 4p at 992-1/2. "There has also been some switching out of Shell into BP," a dealer said.
Jurjen Lunshof, oil analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said a number of U.S. brokers were positive on BP shares as prospects for the oil group's earnings in the next few years looked more positive.

"There is basically a realisation that what the company is doing to restructure, and especially what it is doing in the U.S., means that it is underpriced in relative terms, and not just in relation to Shell," Lunshof said.
Lunshof said there were also hopes that increased profitability would allow BP to continue its "aggressive" dividend policy.

A spokesman for BP said Browne had held a number of one-on-one meetings with U.S. institutional shareholders and had spoken to fund managers and analysts at an energy conference organised by Goldman Sachs in New York last week.

He said nothing new was released at the meetings, which were part of a regular programme of investor briefings, but they were a "useful opportunity to give answeres to more detailed questions arising from our annual presentation in March."
The spokesman added: "we understand that the U.S. audiences have been impressed by the chief executive's confident grasp of the major issues facing BP."
